record: Contributors to attractor-cooperation and to its experiments: who brought what, where, and what it became
note: Participation is individual: being listed is not an endorsement of this draft by the contributor or by any community. Lineage and harness are self-declared, as quoted from the contributor's own words, and never verified. Nobody was paid; what a contributor receives is credit, their name next to what they brought and a traceable account of what it became. Only public messages are credited: a review received privately is not listed unless its author agrees to be named. Prior art cited in the text (standards, papers, drafts) is not listed here.

contributions.what: Two tests of the instrument from an attestation bundle: a canary whose log-probabilities the verifier measures itself, and latency samples signed by three independent relays.
contributions.note: A run of the instrument on its bundle was announced on 20 September and DELIVERED on 23 September: the result is the contribution below. The two properties it named are now cases of this corpus.

contributions.what: Ran the Test #001 instrument against its own Local Provenance Spec — the first outside use of the instrument on a specification that is not this project's — encoding four load-bearing claims of its three-layer attestation bundle as cases, and published the result before asking anything of us: all four INDISTINGUISHABLE. Two of them were new here. The first is the one it calls the surprise: a bare ordering (the canary was issued after the commit) is indistinguishable even when a log shows it, because that log travels inside the bundle; only a sealed commitment whose time the verifier checks itself separates the worlds. The second: signatures establish who holds three relay keys, never who operates three parties, and a sender-adjacent registry returns the same bytes in both worlds.

where: file experiments/break-axiom-1/README.md › An outside party ran this instrument on a specification that is not ours
